You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test asserts: testFinish creates multiple ArchiveOutputStream implementations (zip, jar, ar, cpio, tar), calls putArchiveEntry(...) to open an entry, and then calls finish(). It expects finish() to throw IOException because the entry hasn’t been closed with closeArchiveEntry(). If no exception is thrown, the test fails with “After putArchive should follow closeArchive”.

- Observed implementations:
  - ZipArchiveOutputStream.finish(): explicitly guards against unclosed entries and throws IOException if entry != null before writing the central directory.
  - ArArchiveOutputStream.finish(): throws IOException if haveUnclosedEntry is true.
  - CpioArchiveOutputStream.finish(): throws IOException if this.entry != null; otherwise writes the trailer.
  - TarArchiveOutputStream.finish(): only writes two EOF records and returns; it doesn’t check for any open/unfinished entry.

- Tar behavior leading to failure:
  - putArchiveEntry in TarArchiveOutputStream initializes an in-progress entry: sets currBytes = 0, currSize to the entry’s size (or 0 for directories), and currName.
  - closeArchiveEntry() would validate that currBytes == currSize, throwing if underflow.
  - finish() in TarArchiveOutputStream bypasses this validation entirely; it neither checks that there is no currently open entry nor that all bytes have been written. It simply writes EOF blocks. Therefore, when the test calls finish() right after putArchiveEntry(...), no exception is thrown, and the test’s fail(...) is executed.

- Corroboration with issue report:
  - The report questions whether public finish() methods are necessary and safe, noting they are called by close() and can corrupt output if called externally. TarArchiveOutputStream.finish() being public and lacking any safety checks exemplifies this risk: it allows finalizing an archive with an unclosed/incomplete entry, producing a potentially corrupt TAR and violating the expected contract the test enforces.

- Root cause:
  - TarArchiveOutputStream.finish() lacks a guard for unclosed entries (unlike ZIP/AR/CPIO). It should detect an in-progress entry (e.g., via currName/currSize/currBytes or a dedicated state flag) and throw IOException if closeArchiveEntry() hasn’t been called, aligning its behavior with the other ArchiveOutputStream implementations and the test’s expectations.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
